title: web: visual redesign with one visual language for graph nodes
description:
Owner feedback: 'right now the UI is very ugly.' The implementer may choose the changes to make, but one requirement is fixed: a unified visual language for the nodes in the graph. At the aggregate level the only special nodes are the inputs, the prediction (ŷ) and the loss (L). Every other piece (Linear, activations, Feature, Dropout, Add, link pieces, loss primitives, scalar weights/sums from tinker-9io) uses one node style.

Required:
- One node component used for all ordinary pieces, in both layer and neuron views: same shape, corner radius, fill and border, port style (inputs on one side, outputs on the other, same dot size and hit target), name label (tinker-71r), an optional small glyph or formula for the operation, and a consistent spot for secondary info (width, settings). The type is told apart by the glyph and name, not by a different shape or colour per type.
- Three special kinds with distinct but related styling: inputs (data entering: x columns and target y), the prediction ŷ, and the loss L. Under graph v2 (tinker-8xw), ŷ and L are role pins, so the pins carry the special style; until then the Output and Loss pieces do.
- Wires: one style; states (selected, issue, drop target) consistent; width labels styled as diagnostics.
- States applied the same way to every node: selected, issue, locked, drop target, hover/pressed.

Implementer's choice (propose in the PR with before/after screenshots): typography (one UI font and scale), spacing grid, colour palette (light and dark, colour-blind-safe, contrast AA), panel and region headers, top bar and training bar polish, results panels framing, palette look (palette entries should preview the node style they create), icons. Keep the 32 px touch targets and the s10 viewports.

Relationships: this bead defines the design tokens and node component. tinker-t6o (control vs diagnostic language) and tinker-71r (block names) build on it and depend on it. tinker-8xw.4 (role pins and region shading) and tinker-mit (KaTeX) must use its components. Document the visual language (tokens, node anatomy, special kinds, states) in CONTRACTS s10 so later beads follow it.
acceptance_criteria: A node anatomy and tokens spec documented in CONTRACTS s10; every ordinary piece renders through one shared node component (code check: no per-type shapes); inputs, ŷ and L visibly special and consistent; selected, issue, locked, drop and hover states uniform; before/after screenshots at the s10 viewports in light and dark, which the owner reviews; contrast checked (AA); no gesture or hit-target regressions (existing browser test suite).

title: scalar-level building: x_i nodes, weights, sum; show a Linear layer is the same thing
description:
Owner request: today the canvas shows layers (for example an 8 -> 1 Linear), but students should start with individual scalars. Each input column x_i is its own node; the student attaches a weight to each (w_i * x_i), sums them and adds a bias b, building linear regression ŷ = Σ w_i x_i + b by hand. It must be clear that a Linear layer can be written this way.

Builds on the graph v2 epic (tinker-8xw: arbitrary graph, primitives, ŷ/L roles).

Pieces (core registry + engine + web):
- Column node: one input column x_i (split from Input; Input becomes a group of columns, or columns are first-class).
- Scalar weight: a learnable scalar times its input (one parameter), drawn as a labelled edge or small piece showing w_i and its value; hand-settable like neuron-view edges.
- Sum: adds any number of inputs (variadic ports, or chained binary adds; decide which).
- Bias: a learnable scalar added (one parameter).
- Each must be exact against PyTorch: new fixtures for scalar regression, which must equal nn.Linear(d, 1) with the same numbers.

Showing the equivalence (core of the request):
- 'Group into Linear': select the weighted-sum subgraph (the w_i * x_i edges into a Sum, plus an optional bias) and collapse it into a Linear piece. The parameters carry over exactly (W column = the w_i, b = the bias), and the loss and fit are unchanged (test).
- 'Expand to scalars': the reverse on a Linear (out = 1, and possibly out > 1 as several sums) into scalar pieces with the same values.
- Animated or side-by-side transition, so students see that the box is the same computation (probably through the neuron view, which already draws units and weight edges). A label showing ŷ = Σ_i w_i x_i + b ⇄ ŷ = W x + b (rendered with the LaTeX bead tinker-mit if it has landed).
- A starting preset or default graph at scalar level (for example 2–3 columns, linear regression) so students start there.

Open questions for the owner before building:
1. Is the scalar view a separate grain (alongside Layers | Neurons), or are scalar pieces ordinary graph pieces that the student builds with, with a group/expand action between them and Linear? The second is the coordinator's suggestion: the graph really contains the scalars.
2. Does expand/group also apply to hidden layers (a Linear d -> k as k sums), or only the final linear-regression layer at first?
3. Should weights be pieces (boxes) or labelled wires? Labelled wires read most like the maths; pieces are easier to tap on a tablet.

Contract impact: CONTRACTS s2/s3 (new piece types, group/expand edits), s4 (widths for scalar nodes), s7 (engine pieces), s8 (group/expand edits as one undo step each), s10 (UI), s11 (fixtures). Probably split into core, engine, web and presets beads once the questions are answered. Risk: high.

title: loss spikes at regular intervals late in training
description:
Owner report with screenshot: after training to a certain point, the loss curve shows sharp spikes at fixed, evenly spaced intervals (the curve is otherwise flat near its minimum; each spike decays back within a few steps). Suspected numerical issue.

First step: reproduce, recording the exact settings (dataset, n, graph, optimizer, lr, batch size, standardise, seed). Ask the owner for theirs if a repro isn't obvious. Then find which hypothesis holds; each has a quick discriminating test:
1. Adam near convergence: when gradients become tiny, the second-moment estimate v decays faster than m and the update m/(sqrt(v)+eps) briefly blows up. This gives classic periodic spikes late in training. Test: does it happen with SGD/momentum at the same lr? Does a larger eps (1e-7 or 1e-6) or a smaller lr remove it? Compare with PyTorch Adam on the same graph and data in float64 and float32 (the tools/torch-ref setup).
2. Mini-batch epoch boundary: batchSchedule keeps a partial last batch, so once per epoch a tiny batch gives a noisy, large loss and step. Test: is the spike period equal to stepsPerEpoch? Does full batch or a batch size dividing nTrain remove it? Is the spike only in the per-batch series, not trainFull?
3. float32 precision at very small loss: loss ~1e-7 relative to the parameter scale; check whether the spikes are real (also in val and trainFull) or a plotting artefact (log scale, decimation min/max, which keeps maxima).
4. Something periodic in the app: valEvery cadence, history decimation above 20k points, the frame/publish cadence (speed x frames), or the frame stalls bug (tinker-xqp). Check the spike period in steps against these.
Fix depends on the cause. Adam: maybe expose eps or clamp, documented; mini-batch: drop or merge the partial last batch (change batchSchedule; CONTRACTS s6); plot artefact: fix decimation. Add a regression test that would have caught it.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified with evidence (spike period vs the hypotheses, the setting that removes it, PyTorch comparison if numerical); fix or documented behaviour agreed with the owner; regression test; screenshot of the curve after the fix.
notes:
Owner: the spikes go away with SGD. That points to hypothesis 1 (Adam, or possibly momentum, near convergence), not the mini-batch boundary or a plot artefact. Next: confirm which optimizer the owner was using; check that PyTorch Adam on the same graph, data and lr also spikes (float32 and float64). If torch spikes too, it is genuine Adam behaviour (the second-moment estimate v decays as gradients vanish, so the step m/(sqrt(v)+eps) jumps), not an engine bug. Then the owner decides: keep it (it's real), or mitigate (larger eps such as 1e-6, an AMSGrad variant, or lr decay). Any mitigation is a CONTRACTS s7 change and must keep the Adam fixture within tolerance or get a new fixture.
Owner decision: damp Adam by default. Pick the mechanism by evidence: compare a larger eps (e.g. 1e-6 or 1e-7), AMSGrad, and a mild lr decay on the spike repro and on the existing fixtures. Choose the smallest change that removes the periodic spikes without slowing normal training noticeably, make it the default Adam, and record the choice and why in CONTRACTS s7 and docs. If it changes Adam numerics, update tools/torch-ref/gen.py to the same variant and regenerate the Adam fixture (never hand-edit), keeping the 1e-4 tolerance. Note in the UI or docs only if the owner wants (no lesson text).
Owner decision (2026-11-18), after PR #44 measured the running-max-nu fix at 3-7x slower on presets: keep plain Adam; document the spikes as real Adam behaviour (torch float32 also spikes; SGD doesn't); keep only the long-run Adam fixture.
close_reason: PR #44 merged. Root cause: plain Adam near convergence (PyTorch float32 Adam spikes too; SGD doesn't). Running-max-nu fix removed spikes but was 3-7x slower on presets; owner chose to keep plain Adam. CONTRACTS s7 documents the behaviour, evidence and measured mitigations; new long-run fixture mlp_tanh_adam_300steps.

title: Arbitrary graph with prediction and loss roles
description:
Owner design (discussion 2026-11-18): the graph is an arbitrary DAG of operations; the user designates one or more nodes as predictions (ŷ) and exactly one node as the loss (L). Model vs objective regions are derived from the roles (ancestors of the ŷ nodes = model; what L needs beyond that = objective) and drawn as shading behind the pieces, never as a fixed layout zone, so they can't contradict the graph and they work with free piece placement (tinker-ong).

Decisions:
- UI: role pins. A short wire stub ending in a pin labelled ŷ or L, attached to a node's output. You move a role by dragging its pin to another node's output (same gesture family as wiring). There is only one L pin, so dropping it elsewhere moves it. Coordinator recommendation, not objected to by the owner; confirm before the web bead starts.
- Every ŷ pin's width must match the dataset target (regression or binary: 1; softmax classification: numClasses), otherwise it gets an analyse issue on the pin. With several ŷ pins the fit plot header picks one (default: the first).
- The Output piece goes away. Sigmoid and softmax become ordinary link pieces, and ŷ is just the pin.
- A graph with no ŷ pin still trains if L is valid; the fit plot says 'No prediction selected.'
- The loss can be built from primitives: per-example vs single-number shapes, an explicit Mean reduction, L must be a single number that depends on at least one parameter. The weight penalty becomes graph structure (a Weights node reads a Linear's W, then norm, scale, add), drawn as a dashed parameter wire. The 5 current losses become ready-made groups that expand to primitives.
- Numerical stability: the engine pattern-matches sigmoid -> log loss and softmax -> cross-entropy into fused stable forms. The diagram stays semantic.

Big contract change: CONTRACTS s2-s4, s7-s9, s11, s12. Graph version 2 with migration from version 1 (files, presets, fixtures).

title: engine: patch jax-js 0.1.27 trace-stack leak (partialEvalFlat)
description: Found in PR #27 (tinker-klv). In @jax-js/jax 0.1.27 dist/index.js, partialEvalFlat calls newMain(PartialEvalTrace), which pushes onto the module-level traceStack, and never pops it; newMain returns an object with [Symbol.dispose]() that pops, but nothing calls it. Every traced valueAndGrad, once per compiled model, therefore keeps its Kernel/AluExp/JaxprTrace/PartialEvalTracer objects alive. About 0.32 MB per compile+2 steps, about 1.1 MB more with trainMany. The web app recompiles on every edit. Owner decision: patch locally with pnpm patch (reversible; drop it on upgrade) and draft an upstream issue for the owner to post. Fix: pop the trace frame after the traced function and graph extraction finish (try/finally or using), matching how the library uses newMain elsewhere. Check traceStack length returns to its prior value, and check jvp/vjp/grad/jit/vmap still work (full engine suite + fixtures). Owns patches/@jax-js__jax@0.1.27.patch, the pnpm patchedDependencies entry in the root package.json, an engine test, and a short section in docs/spike.md. Risk: high (patching the numeric library).
acceptance_criteria: pnpm patch applied and committed; a test shows traceStack length (or RSS) flat over 1000 compile+step+disposeModel cycles, where main grows about 0.3 MB per cycle; all engine tests and fixtures pass; draft upstream issue text (repro + one-line fix) in docs/jax-js-upstream-issue.md for the owner to post; CONTRACTS s7 notes the patch.
notes: From PR #27 review: (1) tighten dispose.test.ts's loose RSS bound (1.5 GB/1000 cycles) to a named constant around 100 MB/1000 cycles after the fix, preferably measuring heapUsed after gc() with vitest --expose-gc, and assert traceStack depth returns to baseline if it can be read. (2) Re-check the CONTRACTS s7 bullet saying random ops / np.take index arrays leave a constant buffer per compiled model that is never freed; it may be stale now that jits are disposed. (3) Pre-existing: if startTraining throws inside trainSlice resync's try, the Params from fromHost leak; dispose them in the catch.
close_reason: PR #33 merged. pnpm patch of @jax-js/jax 0.1.27 (patches/@jax-js__jax@0.1.27.patch, patchedDependencies in pnpm-workspace.yaml; dist/index.js + index.cjs): partialEvalFlat pops its trace frame (try/finally); Jaxpr.getHash hashes nested Jaxprs by content so jitCompileCache keys are stable; vmap/jvp/transpose Jaxpr caches are WeakMaps. Heap growth per 1000 compile cycles 1060 MB -> 1 MB. Reviewer: 21 single-setting variants bit-identical across shared/fresh processes (no wrong cache hits reachable). Draft upstream issue in docs/jax-js-upstream-issue.md for the owner to post; re-check the patch on any jax-js upgrade.

title: PyTorch reference fixtures: generator script and committed JSON
description:
The ground truth the engine is tested against (SPEC "Correctness"). A uv script builds each case in PyTorch on fixed inputs and writes the expected predictions, loss, gradients and optimizer trajectories as JSON in the CONTRACTS.md section 11 format.

Cases (one fixture file each; small: n = 5 to 8 rows, widths 1 to 4):
- linear with and without bias; d = 1 and d = 2.
- each activation (sigmoid, tanh, relu, gelu) between two Linears. GELU: torch default (erf form); note in the PR whether jax-js gelu is erf or tanh form if you can tell from its d.ts.
- output links: identity, sigmoid, softmax (width 2).
- each loss: squared_error, absolute_error, huber (delta 1 and 0.5), log_loss (sigmoid output, BCEWithLogits on logits), cross_entropy (softmax output, class-index targets, CrossEntropyLoss on logits), and squared_error on a sigmoid output.
- weight penalty L2 and L1 with lambda 0.1, applied to Linear weights only (explicit added term, not weight_decay; biases excluded).
- feature: degree 3 with sin, cos and products on d = 2.
- add: skip connection lin1 -> act -> lin2 plus lin1 -> add.b.
- dropout p = 0.5 with a fixed mask written to `expect.dropoutMask` (torch output computed with that mask and 1/(1-p) scaling).
- optimizers: 5 full-batch steps of sgd, sgd momentum 0.9, adam (torch defaults) on a 2-layer tanh MLP; record params after 5 steps and the 5 losses.
- a two-parameter model (1 weight, 1 bias) for the loss-surface view.

title: web: render math with LaTeX (KaTeX) instead of Unicode
description:
Owner request: 'can we get latex rendering instead of unicode?'

Math is currently Unicode text in: canvas piece drawings (drawings/output.tsx ŷ, loss.tsx δ and the λ penalty tag, feature.tsx x..x^d, activation.tsx σ/tanh/ReLU/GELU symbols), the Inspector, the bias²/variance readout (results/ResampleOverlay.tsx), pin labels (results/pinsModel.ts, Pins.tsx), axis/legend labels in the canvas-2D plots, and possibly preset prompts (presets/PromptLine.tsx). UI multiplication signs like 'Resample × 20' are not math and stay as text.

Approach to decide in the bead:
- Use KaTeX (small, fast, synchronous; no network, so fonts are bundled locally, which also suits the later offline/PWA bead). One shared <Tex> component plus a tex-to-string cache.
- SVG canvas pieces: KaTeX outputs HTML, so either embed it via <foreignObject> (check hit-testing, scaling with the layer/neuron view transforms, text legibility rules (legibleAt), and Safari/iPad foreignObject quirks), or pre-render KaTeX to an image/SVG per label. Measure the cost on graphs with many pieces and during Run (labels must not re-render per frame).
- Canvas-2D plots (FitPlot, LossCurves, LossSurface): canvas can't draw KaTeX directly, so put axis titles and legends in an HTML overlay positioned over the canvas, or draw cached rasterised labels.
- Preset prompts: decide whether $...$ in prompt text is rendered (prompts are data shown verbatim; if rendered, escape everything else; no HTML injection).
- Light and dark: KaTeX inherits currentColor.
Bundle size: report the added gzipped size.

title: web: unexplained 600-700 ms frame stalls during Run at high speed
description: Found in PR #19 review and follow-up: at speed 50 the training loop shows 600-700 ms gaps about every 1.7 s (roughly every 3000 steps); about 117 ms at speed 10. No rAF callback or long task exceeds 50 ms, --disable-gpu does not change it, and an idle page has none. A headless CDP trace came back empty. Suspect GC or Wasm memory growth tied to allocation (toHost every frame, batch arrays per step). Needs a headed Chrome performance profile (or --trace-gc) to find the cause, then a fix (for example reuse buffers, or publish host less often). Owns packages/web/src/state/trainSlice.ts (perf only). Risk: normal.
acceptance_criteria: Cause identified with a profile; at speed 50 no frame gap over 100 ms during 60 s of Run in headed Chrome on the SPEC example; liveArrays still flat.
close_reason: PR #49 merged. Cause: jax-js 0.1.27 Wasm backend did new WebAssembly.Instance per sync kernel dispatch (~44k/s at speed 50; 654k SyncInstantiate in 15 s trace); main-thread RunTasks of ~500 ms. Fix: pnpm patch caches program.kernelFunc (memory is created once per backend; worker path already caches). After: 0 gaps >100 ms in 60 s headed Chrome, throughput ~2x, liveArrays flat. Regression test engine/test/instances.test.ts (fails without patch: 6200 instances). Upstream jax-js issue not filed.

title: engine: dispose compiled models (free jit caches)
description: Each compile builds jitted predict/eval/step functions that are never disposed (no model disposal in the Engine interface). The PR #14 review measured about 0.19 MB per compiled model, and PR #18 found that jitted functions hold their captured constants. jax-js jit(...) returns a function with .dispose() that frees them. The web app recompiles on every edit and lr change. Add Engine.disposeModel(model), or dispose the previous model's jitted functions on recompile. This is a CONTRACTS s7 change: update s7 and the web engine.ts caller (tinker-27m.2) to dispose the old model when it compiles a new one. Owns packages/engine/src/index.ts, compile.ts, types.ts and the web engine.ts call site. Risk: high (use-after-dispose).
acceptance_criteria: Compiling and disposing 1000 models keeps liveArrays flat and RSS bounded. Using a disposed model throws one plain sentence. The web recompile path disposes the old model. CONTRACTS s7 updated.
notes: From PR #19 review: the plug point is web/src/state/trainSlice.ts resync, where 'rt.model = null' drops the old model without disposing it. Dispose it after disposeState(). restoreBest reuses the model, so it must not dispose. stopLoop() runs first, so there is no use-after-dispose there.
close_reason: PR #27 merged. Engine.disposeModel(model) frees predict/eval/step, trainMany and lossGrid jits (registered in Internals.disposables); every model-taking method throws 'This model was disposed.' before consuming args; double dispose no-op; Params/TrainStates stay valid arrays. Web resync disposes the old model and a compiled-but-unstarted one. Does NOT reduce RSS: jax-js 0.1.27 partialEvalFlat trace-stack leak (~0.32 MB/compile) - tinker-d7c. many.test.ts timeout 60 s.
